text:
maya: Heads up — saw a regression on canary after the new continuous-batching tweak. p95 for short prompts jumped from ~85ms -> ~140ms.

devin: ugh, I saw that in the dashboard. looks like short-prompt batches are getting merged into bigger batches more often?

sam: quick profiler dump: 
```
CPU: kernel_select.hotpath %
  matmul_fp16_fast: 12.1
  matmul_generic: 47.8
KV cache hit ratio by bucket:
  short(<=32): 72%
  mid(33-128): 54%
  long(>128): 18%
queueing: avg wait per req (ms): short=28 mid=42 long=110
```

maya: interesting — matmul_generic is still dominating for short prompts on the canary GPU. suspect kernel selection is falling back when batch composition mixes decode-rate classes.

tess: the new admission policy lowered token_budget_target to 40 for cost reasons. that might be forcing more heterogeneous batches.

laura: can you paste the current admission config for the canary?

sam: sure — current config: 
```
admission:
  token_budget_target: 40
  bucket_classifier:
    by_length: [0,32,128,inf]
    decode_rate_buckets_ms: [0,15,40,inf]
  allow_cross_bucket_merge: true
  timeout_ms: 50
```

devin: hm allow_cross_bucket_merge=true is the culprit. mixing a 6ms-decode request with a 30ms one forces kernel fallback and kv-prefetch thrash.

zach: agreed. proposal: disable cross-bucket merge for short bucket, bump token_budget_target for short to 64, and tighten length threshold to 24 for the ultra-short path. quick A/B.

maya: makes sense. expected effect: fewer mixed batches -> more specialized kernel selection -> p95 drop for shorts. any downside? throughput might drop a bit if we underutilize batch slots.

tess: tradeoff is predictable though. we can try a canary with these changes: 
```
admission:
  token_budget_overrides:
    short: 64
    mid: 40
    long: 32
  bucket_classifier:
    by_length: [0,24,96,inf]
  allow_cross_bucket_merge: false  # only for short->others
```

laura: add to that: prefer kernel hint for short bucket: math_kernel_hint: fp16_fast if avg_seq_len<=24 and avg_decode_ms<=12

sam: I'll run the perf-suite against the canary with a 12h window and replay typical traffic with replay-bot.

perf-bot: scheduled replay: canary-2198765432-replay, workload: prod-mix-2026-03-17, ETA: ~45m

devin: for measurement, focus on these metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, kernel-switch rate, kv-hit ratio, and per-batch heterogeneity (stddev of seq_len).

maya: also log the kernel selection decisions per batch (one-line JSON per batch is fine). we need to be able to correlate kernel fallback events with latency spikes.

zach: if this fixes p95 without sacrificing >6% throughput, we can roll to 10% traffic. otherwise try an intermediate config: allow_cross_bucket_merge only when decode-rate bucket equal.

tess: running the canary now. replay-bot will post results here when done.

replay-bot: replay complete. preliminary numbers:
  short p95: 138ms -> 89ms (after changes)
  short p50: 58ms -> 45ms
  tokens/sec: -3.4%
  kernel-switch-rate (batches/sec): -62%
  kv-hit short: 72% -> 75%

maya: nice improvement on p95, kernel-switch rate drop looks promising. small throughput hit as expected.

devin: please post a small diff for the admission policy so infra can canary the change in config repo. I'll tag for review.

sam: created PR: https://git.internal/r/inference-configs/pulls/482 (admission: short overrides + kernel hint + no-cross-merge).

laura: quick note — we should add a metric alert: if short p95 > 120ms for >5m then rollback to previous admission.

zach: can we also run a microbenchmark for pure short homogeneous workload to verify we hit the fast fp16 kernel? I can run that separately.

tess: started short-only microbench, results: avg decode_ms=9.7, kernel selected=matmul_fp16_fast, p95=48ms, kv-hit=78%

maya: excellent. next steps: 1) land PR after reviews, 2) schedule 10% rollout for 6h with alert, 3) monitor throughput and cost, 4) follow up on mid-bucket thresholds after we collect more telemetry.

devin: assigned follow-up: I'll run a sweep over token_budget targets [48,64,80] for short on a small cluster to find sweet spot.

sam: logging done. will keep this channel updated. thanks all :thumbsup:
